# Neo.util.KeyNavigation has no unit spec

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

`Neo.util.KeyNavigation` (`src/util/KeyNavigation.mjs`, 217 lines) turns a component's `keys` config into keydown handlers. `src/component/Base.mjs:1292` (`beforeSetKeys`) creates one for every component that sets `keys`, and `src/grid/View.mjs:93` gives every grid view one, into which its selection model registers its Up and Down handlers.

## The Problem

- No unit spec covers it. At `fbb9c4da19`, `git grep -l KeyNavigation -- test` returns nothing.
- Its key matching has rules a regression would break silently: matching ignores case, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` and `ArrowUp` match listeners named `Down`, `Left`, `Right` and `Up`, a space matches `Space`, and a keydown that carries no `key` (Chrome's auto-fill sends one) is ignored.

## The Architectural Reality

- `parseUpperCaseKey(key)` (`:126`) maps the space and the four arrow names; every other key passes through.
- `parseKeys(value)` (`:97`) turns the object form `{Enter: 'onEnter', scope: ...}` into `[{fn, key, scope}]` entries, with the scope defaulting to the component's id. An array passes through unchanged, and so does an object while no component is set.
- `register(component)` (`:151`) stores the component's id, parses `keys`, and adds one `keydown` DOM listener whose `bubble` is `keyDownEventBubble`.
- `onKeyDown(data)` (`:70`) calls every matching entry's `fn`, either a function or a method name on its `scope`. A `scope` given as a string is looked up with `Neo.get()`. A method the scope lacks is skipped without an error.
- `removeKey(config)` and `removeKeys(items)` (`:170`, `:191`) remove the first entry equal to a config (`Neo.isEqual`); a non-array `items` is ignored.
- Unit specs live under `test/playwright/unit/` and mirror the source path. `test/playwright/unit/util/` holds the neighbours.

Design authority: n/a — calls no existing behavior wrong.

## The Fix

Add `test/playwright/unit/util/KeyNavigation.spec.mjs`, pinning the current behaviour. No source change.

Current behaviour, run on 2026-11-16 at `fbb9c4da19`:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `parseUpperCaseKey(' ')`, `parseUpperCaseKey('ARROWDOWN')`, `parseUpperCaseKey('ARROWUP')` | `'SPACE'`, `'DOWN'`, `'UP'` (`ARROWLEFT` and `ARROWRIGHT` likewise) |
| `parseUpperCaseKey('ENTER')` | `'ENTER'` |
| `register(component)` with `keys: {Enter: 'onEnter', Down: 'onDown'}` | `keys` becomes `[{fn: 'onEnter', key: 'Enter', scope: <component id>}, {fn: 'onDown', key: 'Down', scope: <component id>}]`, and one `keydown` listener is added with `bubble: false` |
| `parseKeys({scope: 'my-scope', Escape: 'onEsc'})`, component set | `[{fn: 'onEsc', key: 'Escape', scope: 'my-scope'}]` |
| `parseKeys([{key: 'Enter', fn: 'onEnter', scope: 'x'}])` | the same array |
| `onKeyDown({key: 'enter'})` with an `Enter` entry | calls it once |
| `onKeyDown({key: 'ArrowDown'})` with a `Down` entry | calls it once |
| `onKeyDown({key: ' '})` with a `Space` entry whose `fn` is a function | calls the function |
| `onKeyDown({})` | calls nothing |
| `removeKey(config)`, config equal to an entry | removes that entry; a config matching nothing leaves `keys` as it was |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The spec pins `parseUpperCaseKey()` for the space, the four arrow names, and one key that passes through unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2: The spec pins `parseKeys()` and `register()`: the object form becomes `{fn, key, scope}` entries whose scope defaults to the component's id, an explicit `scope` wins and does not become an entry itself, and an array passes through unchanged. A plain object with an `id` and an `addDomListeners()` that records its argument is enough as the component.
- [ ] AC-3: The spec pins `onKeyDown()`: matching ignores case, the arrow names and the space map to `Down`/`Up`/`Left`/`Right`/`Space`, a function `fn` and a method-name `fn` are both called with the keydown data as their first argument, a keydown without `key` calls nothing, and a method the scope lacks raises no error.
- [ ] AC-4: The spec pins `removeKey()` and `removeKeys()`.
- [ ] AC-5: The spec passes with `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/util/KeyNavigation.spec.mjs`, and no file under `src/` changes.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to `src/util/KeyNavigation.mjs`. Two things seen while probing stay as they are and unpinned: `add()` before `register()` throws a `TypeError` today (`keys` is still `null` or the unparsed object), and `unregister()` is a `todo`.
- `toJSON()`.

## How to start

- Read `src/util/KeyNavigation.mjs` and one neighbour in `test/playwright/unit/util/` for the setup lines (`Style.spec.mjs` is short).
- `onKeyDown()` reads the component through `Neo.getComponent()`, which `src/manager/Component.mjs` defines. Import that module in the spec, or the call throws `Neo.getComponent is not a function`.
- In `onKeyDown()` tests, pass the scope object itself rather than an id string: a string scope is looked up with `Neo.get()`, which finds only registered instances.
- Run unit tests only through the config above, never a bare `npx playwright test`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` explains how to claim the issue and open the pull request.
